title: India slump to 116 for six, 240 behind, after Akash Deep's five-for in Christchurch
dek: New Zealand made 356 on day two of the second Test, then took six wickets in India's reply. Dhruv Jurel is unbeaten on 7 going into day three.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India finished the second day of the second Test at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on 116 for six, 240 runs behind New Zealand's 356, after their top order fell to a disciplined pace attack. Akash Deep had earlier taken five for 99 to end New Zealand's innings, but dropped catches and missed run-out chances let the hosts add 110 for their last five wickets.

Dhruv Jurel was unbeaten on 7 at stumps. Washington Sundar, who batted 60 balls for 10, edged Nathan Smith to Tom Latham at second slip off the last ball of the day; the catch was upheld by the third umpire. India need 41 more runs to avoid the follow-on: New Zealand can enforce it with a first-innings lead of 200 or more.

## How India's innings unfolded

Matt Henry bowled Yashasvi Jaiswal for a duck in the first over. Devdutt Padikkal made a brisk 21 off 20 balls before edging Kyle Jamieson to wicketkeeper Tom Blundell, and captain Shubman Gill was caught by Latham at second slip off Jamieson for 17, leaving India 59 for three at tea.

K.L. Rahul, who made 136 in the first Test, ground out 25 off 80 balls, surviving an edge that fell short of third slip, before Jacob Duffy had him caught by Devon Conway. Rishabh Pant hit 23 before he sliced Duffy to Jamieson on the backward-point boundary. India were 104 for five when Rahul fell and lost Sundar with 12 more added.

## How New Zealand's innings ended

New Zealand resumed on 246 for five. Anshul Kamboj had Glenn Phillips caught behind without adding to his overnight 36, and Akash Deep took a return catch to remove Smith for 26 and dismissed Jamieson for 19. Padikkal dropped a straightforward chance at gully that would have given Akash Deep his fifth wicket earlier.

Blundell, playing his 50th Test, batted 211 balls for 89, with 10 fours, before he was caught on the fine-leg boundary by Akash Deep off debutant Gurnoor Brar shortly after lunch. Henry hit 19 before he was the last man out, caught behind, in the 117th over. Tom Latham had made 59 on the first day.

Akash Deep finished with 5 for 99 from 31.3 overs, his second five-wicket haul in Tests. Brar, playing in place of Prasidh Krishna, took 2 for 78 and Kamboj 2 for 79. Jasprit Bumrah went wicketless in 26 overs.

## The series so far

The first Test in Wellington was drawn. New Zealand made 368 in their first innings, with Henry Nicholls carrying his bat for an unbeaten 175, and India replied with 720 for nine declared, the highest total in any Test in New Zealand. New Zealand then batted out the final day to finish on 239 for five. With the two-match series level, a result in Christchurch would decide it, and India's World Test Championship points are at stake.

## What happens next

Day three starts at 3:30 am IST on Sunday. India's lower order, led by Jurel, will try to get past 156 to avoid the follow-on and cut into the deficit. Figures in this report are from match reports and live scorecards.
